description: This week, the following House and Senate bills and resolutions received final passage and have been sent to the governor: SB 622 creates the Joint Study Committee on Evaluating Escalating Costs in Georgia’s Foster Care System. This committee will have 20 members: 6 from the Senate, 6 from the House, 1 appointed by the governor, and officials from the Dept of Human Services, the Dept of Juvenile Justice, and other related organizations. Costs within the foster care system have risen 159% since 2022, and this study committee will address this problem. Rio’s Law, SB 433, has received final passage. This bill allows individuals with autism or other developmental disabilities to obtain a specialized Autism Spectrum Disorder or Developmental Disability license plate, enabling law enforcement to be aware of the individual's diagnosis so they can interact appropriately. The bill also includes provisions for training law enforcement officers on best practices. HB 1118, Paid Maternal Leave, has received final passage. This bill will increase the number of paid maternal leave weeks from 6 to 9 weeks for state employees, giving moms and babies more time together. Human Trafficking, SB 547 has received final passage. This legislation designates both pimping and pandering as felonies, regardless of whether they are first or subsequent offenses, sending a clear message that Georgia will hold offenders accountable. AI Companion Chatbots, SB 540 was sent to the Governor. This bill establishes safeguards for minors who engage with chatbots, which are designed to simulate relationships. This bill mandates parental control tools and protocols for responding to self-harm prompts. SB 500 will expand the behavioral health workforce database and include more provider licensing boards to help address shortages. SB 503, The Georgia Insurance Fairness Act, updates our state’s insurance laws to enhance consumer protections. This bill will better safeguard those who rent their homes by ensuring that guarantees offered through rental home marketplaces are not classified as property insurance. It will also strengthen oversight of private passenger automobile insurance. Additionally, it extends filing deadlines after declared disasters and sets timelines for processing claims from catastrophic events. Furthermore, it authorizes law enforcement to issue tickets to drivers without valid insurance coverage. SB 472 will ensure school board accountability and allow the State Board of Education to recommend to the governor that local school board members be suspended without pay when the state auditor flags a district for financial mismanagement or misconduct. SB 442 will repeal a noncitizen’s commercial driver’s license once their visa has expired. It will also provide for testing requirements for renewal of commercial drivers’ licenses for noncitizens. SB 150 allows retired public school teachers to return to work and continue receiving their retirement allowance and any post-retirement benefits alongside their teaching compensation, strengthening our teacher workforce. HB 428 addresses the gap where individuals need mental health support but do not require institutional care. This bill will enable the Georgia Dept of Community Health to submit waiver requests to Medicare and Medicaid on behalf of people over 21 who need mental health services and have a history of incarceration, homelessness, or hospitalization. SB 443 establishes an offense for purposefully or recklessly obstructing any highway or street. Individuals who commit this offense will be held civilly liable for any resulting damages.
title: Legislative Week 11 Recap-Rep. Carmen Rice
